title: The Real Reason Tariffs Haven't Raised Your Prices Yet
summary: Argues the 2025 tariffs did not spike prices because firms absorbed about 80 percent in margins, but surveys and Fed data show pass-through reaching about 90 percent by mid-2026, making it the largest tax rise since 1993.

assertions.quote: Fed researchers found evidence of something they called near full pass through with consumers now covering close to 90% of tariff costs
For most of a year, it looked like tariffs were somehow free. They weren't free. They were financed.
businesses absorbed roughly 80% of tariff costs themselves that year, not out of generosity, out of fear.

verdicts.note: Cavallo et al. found retail prices of tariffed goods rose with a lag in 2018-2019, and 2025 surveys showed firms absorbing most of the cost in margins before raising prices.

assertions.quote: That makes it the largest tax increase as a share of the economy since 1993.

verdicts.note: Tax Foundation and Yale Budget Lab both put the 2025 tariffs near 1 percent of GDP, the largest increase since 1993, though court rulings have since trimmed them.

assertions.quote: Core inflation hit 3.2% 2% that March, the highest reading since 2023.

verdicts.note: Fed and Yale Budget Lab estimates attribute several tenths of a point of core goods inflation to tariff pass-through, a real but partial contributor.

Tariffs contributed about 2.9 percentage points to twelve-month inflation in the 67 non-oil consumer goods categories sampled by February 2026, but the estimate is a relative-price effect identified against less-exposed goods and covers goods only (20 percent of the basket), so it does not measure the effect on core CPI as a whole.

assertions.quote: By later that year, it had climbed past 16%, the highest level since 1936.

verdicts.note: Yale Budget Lab put the effective rate near 17 percent in late 2025, the highest since the mid-1930s, before the 2026 court ruling cut it.

The paper states the 2025 tariffs took U.S. import tariffs to their highest levels since the 1930s, with the average statutory rate peaking near 16 percent in September 2025; the duty rate actually collected ran at about two-thirds of the statutory rate.
